program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 2000

source_provenance: Sider Scholar + NCBI PubMed exact-source verification
cumulative PMID collision index covering prior enrichment waves and current branch

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 2000

waves.focus: Small double-blind placebo-controlled trial in persistent allergic rhinitis found high-dose EPA+DHA was safe but did not improve nasal symptoms or quality of life beyond intranasal steroid plus immunotherapy; adjunctive null evidence.

Secondary path analysis of randomized diet-trial data linked higher achieved blood EPA/DHA—especially EPA—to lower pain interference in migraine; mediation/association analysis does not replace the parent randomized outcome interpretation.

Large UK Biobank observational analysis found higher circulating omega-3 associated with lower incident AF while self-reported fish-oil use was neutral after continuous age adjustment; observational biomarker and supplement-use associations should not be treated as randomized safety evidence.

PubMed marks this omega-3 psychological-distress randomized trial as a retracted publication; its efficacy claims must not be used for evidence grading or consumer guidance and are retained only for retraction/citation-integrity tracking.

Secondary analysis of a randomized CAD trial found beetroot-containing interventions changed selected fatty-acid ratios and oxidative markers, with larger shifts in a beetroot-plus-vitamin-C arm; secondary biomarker and combination effects limit clinical interpretation.

Small double-blind crossover study in 11 active men found both beetroot and creatine improved selected velocity measures versus placebo, while beetroot produced distinct heart-rate, oxygenation and HRV effects; acute mechanistic performance study only.

Double-blind randomized pediatric cardiac-surgery trial found preoperative oral L-carnitine was associated with faster normalization of selected liver markers after surgery; perioperative setting and biochemical endpoints limit generalization.

Large pre-post study of a branded hydrolyzed-collagen/B-vitamin/zinc supplement reported improved hair parameters after one month with persistence after washout, but absence of a concurrent control and multi-ingredient product design prevent causal ingredient claims.

Meta-analysis of 25 case-control studies found lower blood/plasma zinc in children and adolescents with autism while hair and urinary zinc were not different; very high heterogeneity and observational design preclude supplementation-efficacy conclusions.

Systematic review/meta-analysis linked higher circulating and dietary selenium with lower ischemic-stroke and stroke-mortality risk, but the evidence is observational and heterogeneous; no supplementation effect can be inferred.

Systematic review describes potential metabolic and cardiovascular harms of excessive zinc exposure and emphasizes dose-dependent risk, interaction and toxicity uncertainty; useful safety context rather than a quantified safe-threshold source.

Systematic review of seven trials found zinc-biofortified staple crops produced inconsistent improvements in zinc biomarkers, with methodological issues including inflammation adjustment and cooking losses; food-biofortification evidence should not be generalized to supplements.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of double- and multi-fortified salt interventions found iron-containing formulations improved hemoglobin overall, but nutrient combinations and food-fortification context prevent translation into single-supplement efficacy.

Open-label randomized study in Filipino preschool children found fortified milk increased nutrient intake and some growth measures but did not significantly improve the primary micronutrient-status endpoints versus habitual diet after 16 weeks.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found weak associations between several micronutrient deficiencies and glycemic-control indices in type 2 diabetes, with stronger signals for magnesium and vitamin D in selected measures; association does not prove supplementation benefit.

Secondary analysis of the multicountry Women First trial found no significant association between maternal selenium status and birth size, prematurity or small-for-gestational-age outcomes and no clear selenium increase from the study supplement.

Systematic review of 13 pediatric chronic-disease studies found probiotics, fatty acids, vitamins, minerals and other supplements often changed biomarkers but produced inconsistent clinical benefits; DMSA raised specific safety concerns.

Narrative review synthesizes omega-3, CoQ10, magnesium and selenium across cardiovascular mechanisms and trials; useful as an evidence map but not independent proof of efficacy because conclusions depend on underlying heterogeneous trials.

Randomized pilot in preschool children found two weeks of nonviable L. salivarius HM6 altered plaque S. mutans/Lactobacillus patterns, but microbiologic outcomes and short follow-up do not establish caries prevention.

Single-arm open-label study found a B. longum BB536 plus lactulose fermented-milk product improved bowel-movement and presenteeism/well-being scores alongside microbiome/metabolite changes; no control group prevents causal inference.

Narrative review describes immune, barrier and antioxidant mechanisms proposed for postbiotics across chronic diseases but emphasizes the need for component-specific human trials; largely mechanistic/heterogeneous evidence.

Twelve-week observational program in 48 adults associated personalized multi-agent protocols with reductions in CRP, homocysteine and other biomarkers, but interventions included multiple nutrients, hormones and peptides without a control group.

Review found inconsistent observational and adjunctive-trial evidence for vitamins/minerals in periodontal disease because of small samples, mixed nutrient combinations, variable doses and heterogeneous outcome measurement.

Preprint meta-analysis of 34 omega-3 RCTs reported increased AF risk mainly in high-CVD-risk populations receiving higher EPA/DHA doses; because the source is a preprint, it remains research-only pending peer-reviewed confirmation.

RCT in 68 migraine patients found eight weeks of flaxseed powder improved headache severity, sleep and headache-related quality of life but not headache frequency or duration; small single trial requires replication.
